# Working in this repository

This repository is a **projection of a literate corpus**. For most crates here
the Markdown document is the source and the `.rs` file is derived from it.

## The one rule

**Never hand-edit a file whose header says `@generated by x0k-tangle`.** The
header names the document it came from. Edit that document and re-tangle; a
hand-edit is silently reverted the next time anyone re-tangles, and
`tools/x0k-guard-generated` refuses it in a pull request.

```sh
cargo run -p x0k-tangle -- tangle knowledge/implementation/<area>/<doc>.md --workspace .
```

Then diff the result. The generated file must equal a fresh tangle
**byte for byte** — formatting included, which is why you must not run
`cargo fmt` or `rustfmt` over a generated file. Reformatting *is* drift.

Going the other way, an edit made to generated code can be stitched back into
its document with `x0k-tangle sync`. That is the supported path when it is
easier to work in the code; it is not a licence to skip the document.

## The gate

`tools/ci` is the whole contract, and any CI runner just calls it: build, test,
clippy and rustdoc with warnings denied, the `deny.toml` supply-chain policy
when `cargo-deny` is installed, then a re-tangle of every document that fails if
the tree changed. Run it before you propose anything.

`rust-toolchain.toml` pins the toolchain that CI and a local run share. The
floor is `rust-version` in the workspace manifest (currently `1.89`), and
clippy's `incompatible_msrv` lint proves it rather than asserting it.

## Everything here is generated

Every `.rs` file in this repository carries an `@generated` header and was
tangled from a document under `knowledge/implementation/`. There is no second
category — no file you edit directly, and so no question about which half of a
crate is authored and which is derived. Change the document, re-tangle.
`PROVENANCE.json` lists the documents that back the code (`literate_docs`), the
crates in the bundle, and what was deliberately held back.

## Documents have types and edges

A folio document opens with a YAML envelope declaring what it *is* (`type`) and
what it points at (`edges`, naming other documents by id). Those names are terms
of the vocabulary in `x0k-ontology/ontology/modules/`. Ids that resolve to
nothing here are expected: this repository is a slice of a larger private
corpus, and an edge into an unpublished document is a dangling reference by
design, not a bug to fix.

## Commands that need the corpus

`weave-region`, `project-repo`, `publish-repo`, and `receive-repo` read the
corpus this repository was projected from and refuse to run here. They are
marked `[corpus-only]` in `x0k-tangle --help`. Everything else works.
